intro_html: Trini curry chicken starts with green seasoning and blooming curry powder in hot oil, and ends with chicken and potatoes swimming in gravy you will want to drink. Each bowl delivers a massive 58 grams of protein for about $1.97. Island flavor, gas station coffee price.
cost_closing_html: About $1.97 a bowl for Trinidadian curry chicken with potatoes. A Caribbean takeout plate runs $13 or more, so this batch saves you roughly $150 versus eating out 14 times.
shop_smart: This recipe leans hard on chicken thighs, 8.5 pounds at about $20.83. That is the biggest protein load in this series per dollar, thighs at $2.45 a pound are hard to beat.
Potatoes stretch the batch at about $2.14 for 10 of them. Pound for pound, potatoes are still the cheapest filling food in the store, use them.
Curry powder, turmeric, cumin, and garam masala look like a long list, but they are jars you buy once. The fresh cash for this batch is basically chicken, potatoes, and an onion.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Blend or finely chop the cilantro, garlic, jalapeno, and half the onion into a rough green seasoning paste. Toss the chicken thighs, cut into large chunks, with the paste and a big pinch of salt. Let it sit at least 15 minutes, longer if you have it.
Stir the curry powder, turmeric, cumin, and garam masala with a few tablespoons of water to make a slurry.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high. Pour in the curry slurry and fry it, stirring, until the water cooks off and the oil separates and the kitchen smells serious, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and remaining onion and stir to coat every piece in the fried curry. Cook 5 minutes, letting the chicken release its own liquid.
Add the potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks, plus enough water to come halfway up. Cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender, the gravy thickens, and the chicken reads 165F, about 25 minutes.
Taste for salt and black pepper, and mash a few potato chunks against the pot wall if you want the gravy thicker.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Portion to that number and each bowl lands at about 577 calories with 58 grams of protein, the highest protein count on this page.

head.keywords: trinidadian curry chicken, trini curry, caribbean chicken recipe, curry chicken meal prep, high protein meal prep, budget curry
steps: Marinate chicken chunks in a blended green seasoning of cilantro, garlic, jalapeno, and onion.
Fry a curry powder and spice slurry in hot oil until the oil separates.
Add chicken and onion and coat in the fried curry.
Add potato chunks and water, then cover and simmer until tender and 165F.
Thicken the gravy, season, and portion into 14 containers.
